detail: While planning V0, nearly committed to building the automated retro loop (v1) before dogfooding it by hand on a real project — build ahead of validation. Corrected: Wizard-of-Oz the loop manually first, then automate only if it produces value.

On the Two Way Invoice Sync dogfood, init.md's emitter (phase 4) wrote CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md with byte-identical content (confirmed via diff -q). Duplication violates token-economy T1, and Claude Code reads ONLY CLAUDE.md while AGENTS.md is the cross-vendor standard. Fixed: AGENTS.md canonical + CLAUDE.md = one-line @AGENTS.md import.

Built the strict-path-guard hook using permissionDecision 'defer' from an unverified claude-code-guide answer. 'defer' is headless-only and wrong for an interactive passive warning (correct: exit 0 + additionalContext, no permissionDecision). Caught by the crossed adversarial review + a grounding pass. Lesson: ground every API claim against the docs before shipping code — even a claim from a sub-agent. voice V2 (verify before asserting) applies to sub-agent output too.

The build plan specified `claude -p --output-format stream-json` for the llm/ adapter without ever running it. Live probing found three errors: stream-json errors without --verbose; a naive invocation inherits the caller's whole ambient config (MCP servers, plugins, SessionStart hooks) costing 140,682 input tokens / $0.84 for a one-word answer versus ~11.4k / $0.03-0.08 hermetic — a 10x cost gap that would have silently destroyed the frugality thesis; and --bare, the obvious fix, forces ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and never reads OAuth, which would lose the subscription cost advantage. Validating risk #1 at Step 0 instead of at integration time was correct. Same class as sig-0003.

Using --system-prompt (replacing rather than appending) made the model leak raw tool-call markup (</parameter>, </invoke>) INTO a schema-valid string field. Native --json-schema validation passed on a payload that was unusable. Empirical proof that the LLM verdict contract needs contamination detection plus validate-and-retry, not just schema validation — the design assumed schema validation would be sufficient. Fixed in core/llm/verdict.ts with the real payload as a regression fixture; --append-system-prompt is now mandatory.

The first contamination check matched a bare ' is unclosed') and turned every front-end review into a retry loop that fails closed. Caught by writing the false-positive test before trusting the guard. Lesson: a guard against garbage needs a test proving it accepts the legitimate case, not only that it rejects the bad one.

ADR-0008's pre-registered kill criterion was measured at Step 0: a correctness lens returned 10/10 correct and unanimous on BOTH a known-good and a known-bad fixture (claude 2.1.225, sonnet, $0.79 for 20 calls). The agent-lens-can-earn-block assumption survives its first test. CAVEAT, recorded so it is not overclaimed: the fixtures are mirror-image and unambiguous (removing vs adding a null check before a dereference). This proves the harness works and the easy case is stable; it does NOT prove stability on borderline diffs, which is where a gate actually lives. Harder fixtures are owed before any lens ships as severity: block.
